captions.instagram:
Most editing time goes on things a command already does.

Transcribe first. Cut on the transcript, not the waveform. Check before you post, not after.

This is an example carousel that ships with Social Studio. Edit it, delete it, or use it as a starting point.
captions.linkedin:
Editing time tends to go on work that is already automatable.

Working from a transcript rather than a waveform means a cut never lands mid-word, and a pre-publish check catches the clipped headline before an audience does rather than after.

This is an example carousel included with Social Studio, an open source tool for building carousels, slideshows and Reels locally.
altText: Slide 1 of 5. Four commands, no editor. No timeline. No scrubbing. These are not advanced. They are just not obvious when you start.
Slide 2 of 5. Step 1: Pull the transcript. Whisper, locally. Terminal showing: $ transcribe clip.mp4; -> clip.srt written in 12s; $ head -3 clip.srt.
Slide 3 of 5. Step 2: Cut the dead air. Silence removal runs on the transcript, not the waveform, so it never clips the start of a word.
Slide 4 of 5. Step 3: Check before you post. Catch it here, not there. Terminal showing: $ check slides.json; ! slide 3: headline clipped; ok: 4 of 5.
Slide 5 of 5. This deck is an example. Edit it, or start a new one.
